Cashback vs Reward Points: Which Actually Saves You More?
When choosing a credit card, one common question is whether cashback or reward points provide better value.

Cashback offers an AED-denominated return on eligible spending, while reward points can provide access to different redemption options. Neither is automatically better: the value you receive depends on your spending habits, the card’s earning structure, applicable fees and how you use your rewards.
The right comparison is therefore not simply the advertised cashback percentage or the number of points earned. It is the actual value you receive from the spending you would normally make.
How Do Cashback and Reward Points Work?
Cashback
Cashback allows you to earn a percentage of your eligible credit card spending as an AED-denominated reward.

For example, if a card offers 5% cashback on an eligible category and you spend AED 1,000, you could earn AED 50. The actual amount will depend on the eligible transactions, applicable cashback rate, minimum spend requirement and cashback cap.
Depending on the card, cashback may be credited automatically or may need to be redeemed as a credit to the card account.
Cashback may be suitable if you:
Prefer a straightforward reward structure
Want to understand the value of your rewards easily
Spend regularly within the card’s eligible cashback categories
Reward Points
Reward points are earned on eligible credit card purchases and accumulated within the card’s rewards programme.
Depending on the programme, points may be redeemed for cashback or statement credit, flights, hotel bookings, vouchers, merchandise or other rewards.
Reward points may be suitable if you:
Want to accumulate points towards a larger reward
Regularly monitor your points balance and expiry dates
The number of points earned does not, by itself, show how valuable the programme is. You must also understand how much those points are worth when redeemed.
Cashback vs Reward Points: Which Provides More Value?
The most useful way to compare cashback and reward points is to calculate their effective value-back rate:
If AED 5,000 in eligible spending earns AED 150 in cashback, the effective value back is 3%.
If the same spending earns points worth AED 200 under the selected redemption option, the effective value back is 4%.
In this example, the points provide greater value. However, if those points are redeemed for an option worth only AED 100, the cashback provides a better return.
Net annual value = Total AED value of rewards received − annual membership fee − applicable reward-related fees

Interest, late-payment charges and other card fees can also outweigh the value of any rewards earned. Rewards provide genuine value only when the card is used responsibly and repayments are made in accordance with the card’s terms.

Review where you already spend the most, such as groceries, dining, travel, fuel, entertainment or online shopping. A card that rewards your normal spending may provide more value than one offering a high rate on categories you rarely use.
Avoid spending more or changing your budget simply to earn additional rewards.

Some accelerated cashback or points rates apply only after a specified monthly spend is achieved. Check whether the requirement is calculated by calendar month or statement period and whether it fits comfortably within your existing budget.
A card may offer an attractive earning rate but limit the maximum cashback or points you can earn. Estimate how quickly your regular spending would reach the cap.
Reward eligibility is often determined by the merchant category code assigned to the transaction. A purchase may therefore earn a different rate if the merchant is classified under another category.

Cash advances, balance transfers, fees, charges, cash-equivalent transactions, refunds and reversals are commonly excluded. Government payments, utilities, digital-wallet transactions and other categories may also earn a reduced rate or no rewards, depending on the card.
For reward points, check:
The minimum number of points required for redemption
Whether points can be used for partial payment
How long points remain valid
The same number of points may provide different AED values depending on how they are redeemed.
Cashback Crediting Conditions

Check whether cashback is credited automatically or requires manual redemption. A cashback or statement credit may reduce your card balance but may not be treated as your required monthly payment. Always follow the payment amount and due date shown on your statement.
How Deem Makes Eligible Spending More Rewarding

Deem Credit Cards allow customers to earn Joy Points on eligible retail transactions. Customers can select either Travel or Lifestyle as their Joy Mode, depending on the categories that best match their spending.
Accelerated Joy Points apply when eligible transactions reach the applicable minimum billed amount within the calendar month:
Accelerated Joy Points by Deem Credit Card
To qualify for accelerated Joy Points, meet the applicable minimum spend within the calendar month:
Deem Titanium Credit Card: Spend at least AED 3,000 and earn up to 50,000 Joy Points per month.
Deem Platinum Credit Card: Spend at least AED 5,000 and earn up to 75,000 Joy Points per month.
Deem World Credit Card: Spend at least AED 7,500 and earn up to 100,000 Joy Points per month.
Earning rates, eligible transactions, spending categories and monthly caps are subject to the Deem Joy Points Programme terms and conditions.
Joy Points can be tracked and redeemed through the Deem Mobile App or Web Portal. Under the current programme terms:
A minimum of 15,000 Joy Points is required for redemption
Joy Points expire 24 months from the month in which they are issued
100 Joy Points are worth AED 0.50 when redeemed for cashback or gift cards and AED 1 when used for other available redemption options
This difference in redemption value is important when calculating the effective return. The maximum number of Joy Points available each month should not be treated as a fixed cashback amount.
Earning rates, merchant categories, exclusions, minimum spend requirements, redemption values and monthly caps are subject to the applicable Deem Joy Points Programme terms and conditions.
How to Get More Value From Your Credit Card Rewards
Choose a card that rewards the categories where you already spend regularly.
Monitor your eligible transactions and rewards throughout the month. This can help you understand whether you are meeting the applicable minimum spend without exceeding your budget.
Once you reach the monthly cap, additional spending may earn rewards at a standard rate or may not generate additional value, depending on the programme.
Redeem Points Carefully
Compare the available redemption options before using your points. A higher-value redemption option can improve your effective return.
Check your rewards balance regularly and redeem points before they expire.

Finance charges, late-payment fees and other costs can quickly outweigh the rewards earned. Paying the full statement balance by the due date is important if you want cashback or reward points to provide genuine value.
There is no universal winner between cashback and reward points.

Cashback may be more suitable for customers who prefer straightforward and predictable value. Reward points may provide greater flexibility—and potentially greater value—when spending matches the accelerated categories and points are redeemed carefully.
Ultimately, the better option is the one that matches your regular spending, budget and preferred way of using rewards without encouraging unnecessary purchases.
Are cashback and reward points the same?
No. Cashback provides an AED-denominated reward based on eligible spending. Reward points must be accumulated and redeemed through the options available under the card’s rewards programme.
How can I calculate the value of my reward points?

Divide the AED value of the selected reward by the number of points required. To calculate your overall value-back rate, divide the AED value received by the eligible amount spent and multiply the result by 100.
Do cashback and reward points expire?

Expiry conditions depend on the card and rewards programme. Some cashback balances and reward points may expire if they are not used within the specified period. Deem Joy Points currently expire 24 months from the month in which they are issued.
Is cashback better for everyday spending?

Cashback may provide better value when your regular expenses fall within the card’s eligible cashback categories. Reward points may provide a higher return if your spending qualifies for accelerated earning rates and you select a higher-value redemption option.
